name: Separation pay
authority: Labor Code art.298: one month’s pay or one month per year of service, whichever is higher, on termination for installation of labour-saving devices or redundancy; art.298–299: half a month per year or one month, whichever is higher, on retrenchment, closure not due to serious losses, or disease. A fraction of at least six months counts as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Labor Code arts.298–299: one month’s pay per year of service (redundancy, the only authorised cause the exit reasons distinguish; a fraction of at least six months counts as a year), never less than one month. Tax: exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(b) as pay for a cause beyond the employee’s control (redundancy or retrenchment), so the class counts toward nothing and no withholding scheme reads it. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the exit fact `termination_cause` chooses the award — labour-saving devices or redundancy one month a year (art.298); retrenchment, a closure not due to serious losses, or disease half a month a year (arts.298–299); a closure due to serious business losses owes none (art.298: the half-month award is for closures "not due to serious business losses").

name: Retirement pay
authority: RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): an employee retiring at 60 to 65 after at least five years’ service, with no retirement plan, is paid half a month’s salary for every year of service — 22.5 days: fifteen days, the five-day service incentive leave and one twelfth of the 13th-month pay — a fraction of at least six months counting as a year. Applied 2026-09-19 (2): RA 7641 (Labor Code art.302): optional retirement from sixty and compulsory at sixty-five, after five years’ service — a person retiring past sixty-five is inside it; retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten workers are outside (`company.facts.small_establishment`). One-half month salary is 22.5 days of the daily rate, the daily rate being the monthly basic on the person’s own factor (365 for the monthly-paid, 313 on a six-day week, 261 on five). Tax: the statutory benefit is exempt under NIRC s.32(B)(6)(a), which is why this class pays the RA 7641 minimum only — any excess over it under a company plan would be tested against RA 4917 (age 50, ten years’ service, BIR-qualified plan). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5): the exemption is its own required entity fact, `company.facts.retirement_exempt_establishment` — RA 7641 exempts retail, service and agricultural establishments of not more than ten employees, a different class from the SIL exemption of any establishment regularly employing fewer than ten (`small_establishment`); a small manufacturer owes retirement pay.

name: Christmas or anniversary gift

authority: RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) (k): benefits under a CBA and a productivity incentive scheme, combined, to ₱10,000 a year: a de minimis benefit, outside compensation to the ceiling; the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (NIRC s.32(B)(7)(e)) — the WTAX part `CBA`, capped over the calendar year.
name: CBA and productivity incentive benefit

authority: RR 2-98 s.2.78.1(A)(3) as amended by RR 11-2018 (and RR 4-2025 for uniforms and achievement awards, from 30 January 2025) (j): a daily meal allowance for overtime work or a night/graveyard shift is de minimis to 25% of the region’s basic minimum wage for each such day (the region’s monthly figure × 12 ÷ 313 is the daily wage the order states). The ceiling bounds the exemption, never the pay: the class pays what the employer keyed, whole. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): the WTAX part `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 25% × the daily minimum wage × `person.period.overtime_days` (the payslip’s dates with overtime or night-window hours); the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018: “benefits given in excess of the maximum amount allowed as de minimis benefits shall be included as part of ‘other benefits’”).

The ceiling bounds the exemption, never the pay: the class pays what the employer keyed, whole. Applied 2026-09-23 (round 5, V): the WTAX part `OT_MEAL` is exempt to 30% × the daily minimum wage × `person.period.overtime_days` (the payslip’s dates with overtime or night-window hours); the excess is an ‘other benefit’ inside the ₱90,000 exclusion (RR 11-2018 s.2.78.1(A)(3) closing paragraph; RMC 50-2018: “benefits given in excess of the maximum amount allowed as de minimis benefits shall be included as part of ‘other benefits’”).
name: Overtime or night-shift meal allowance
